solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A flower will transform these areas

indicators.note: to transform something is to change its shape, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener promises that one bloom will change the look of these beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will transform' rearranges THESE AREAS into the flower's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartsease is a common name for the wild pansy, a small flowering plant.

clue.text: We must top and tail these earthbound creatures

indicators.note: cutting off both ends of the two words, as with beans, leaves the run of letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Flightless birds are told they must stay on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top and tail' drops the first and last letters of WEMUST, which is how the setter hides the birds inside 'We must'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large Australian birds that cannot fly, so they are bound to the earth.

definitions.meaning: to enjoy something greatly, to savour it
a piquant condiment or pickle served with food

explanation.definitionFit: Relish as a verb is to enjoy keenly; as a noun it is a tangy condiment.

definitions.meaning: noticed or caught sight of
marked with spots on the skin

explanation.definitionFit: Spotted means both noticed by the eye and covered in spots, as with a rash.

indicators.note: the university letter leaves the word for an examination, so it is removed

parts.note: an audit is an official examination of accounts

explanation.surface: A student who drops out skips the entrance exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' takes U out of AUDIT. An adit is a horizontal mine entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a near-horizontal passage giving access into a mine, so an entrance.

clue.text: Comes out East and joins up

parts.note: merges means combines or joins together

explanation.surface: Someone from the East appears and signs up.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view, a straightforward synonym.

parts.note: reads as 'warmer, mostly', but the main is the sea, and this is an ocean current that warms the waters it flows through

explanation.surface: Something is, on the whole, a bit warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic word for the open sea, and 'in the main' is not 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic current from the Gulf of Mexico carries warm water to north-west Europe, a warmer in the ocean.

definitions.meaning: aloofness or lack of emotional involvement
a group of troops sent away from the main body on a separate task

explanation.definitionFit: Detachment means aloofness, and in the military a detachment is a unit separated for special duty.

clue.text: French priest one may go to Lourdes to find

definitions.meaning: a French parish priest, the title used in France for a vicar

definitions.text: one may go to Lourdes to find
definitions.meaning: Lourdes is a pilgrimage site where the sick seek miraculous healing

explanation.definitionFit: Curé is a French parish priest; a cure is the healing pilgrims hope for at Lourdes, a French shrine.

clue.text: Parliamentary device that heads off further debate?

definitions.text: Parliamentary device that heads off further debate?

parts.words: Parliamentary device that heads off further debate?
parts.note: a procedure that cuts debate short by a timetable, with 'heads off' also hinting at the French machine that removed heads

explanation.surface: A procedural rule stops politicians arguing any more.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament this is a motion allocating fixed time to a bill, so debate ends at a set point.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary timetable motion that ends debate shares its name with the beheading machine of revolutionary France.

indicators.note: signals that the word affair is only one possible arrangement of these letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Marriage might be described as a binding affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges AFFAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is palm fibre used as a tying material, for example for bundles or plants, so a binding.

definitions.meaning: to dismiss, especially an officer from the armed forces in disgrace
a bank or shop worker handling payments

explanation.definitionFit: To cashier is to dismiss from service; a cashier is the person at the till receiving payment.

parts.note: cons are confidence tricks, swindles
piracy is theft, at sea or of copyright material

explanation.surface: A list of a criminal gang's activities: fraud, stealing and plotting.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy is a secret plot, and intrigue means secret scheming.

clue.text: Appears to accept poetry generating good taste

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: seems means appears to be
lines are verses, so poetry

explanation.surface: Someone seems willing to accept verse as a mark of refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemliness is propriety or decorum, conduct in good taste.

clue.text: Course must be if you steer wrongly

definitions.text: Course must be if you steer wrongly

indicators.note: doing something wrongly means getting it out of order, so the letters of steer are scrambled

explanation.surface: A navigator's warning: if you steer badly you will have to correct your heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges STEER; the whole clue also defines it, since a mis-steered course must be set again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset a course is to set it afresh, which is what a mistaken bearing demands.

clue.text: In retrospect the Internet will irritate or captivate

indicators.note: looking back means reading the word backwards

parts.note: the web is a common name for the Internet
to itch is to irritate the skin

explanation.surface: Looking back, the online world will annoy or enthral you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retrospect' turns WEB into BEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewitch is to enchant or captivate, a close synonym.

clue.text: It's in banks, and also in circulation

definitions.text: It's in banks, and also in circulation

parts.words: It's in banks, and also in circulation
parts.note: suggests money, but describes a body fluid stored in donor banks and pumped round the body

explanation.surface: A riddle about money held in banks and passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' and 'circulation' point to cash, but they also fit donor stores and the body's circulatory system.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood is held in blood banks for transfusion and moves through the body's circulation.

parts.note: sounds like helping or applauding performers, but describes handing out cards at a card table

explanation.surface: Someone helps or applauds the performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hand' is a set of playing cards, not help or applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer distributes cards to each player, giving everyone a hand.

parts.note: née, born, is used before a woman's maiden name
d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A life summed up: born poor and died poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Need means want or destitution, a synonym for poverty.

parts.note: her is a pronoun for a woman
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A woman receives a note and a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Here means present, in attendance, as in answering a register.

clue.text: Doctor joins me in a drink

indicators.note: one piece joins up with another, sitting alongside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician joins the speaker for a glass of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux wine from the Médoc region, so a drink.

clue.text: Man admitting set-up is kind of cross

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: male means a man

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading the word upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man confesses the arrangement left him rather angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' does double duty in the surface as one word; in the down clue 'up' reverses SET. 'admitting' puts that inside MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maltese cross is a cross with four arrowhead-shaped arms, a particular type of cross.

indicators.note: breaking the words smashes their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits they cannot break their grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges ICANNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain is to hold within, as a box holds its contents.

clue.text: Stinker of a place to renovate

indicators.note: renovating means doing a thing over, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A dump of a house is due for a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovate' rearranges PLACETO.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a weasel-like animal known for its foul smell, so a stinker.

definitions.meaning: a person walked over by others
a mat at a door for wiping shoes

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a noun for someone downtrodden, here clued by the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is a mat for wiping shoes, and figuratively someone who lets others walk over them.

definitions.meaning: Billy Bunter, the fat schoolboy of the Greyfriars stories
to move home from one dwelling to another

explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is a comic British schoolboy character; his school year group had this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Remove is a school form name in some British schools; to remove is an old word for moving house.

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a batsman put out by the wicket being broken while running
used up, with none left

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman is dismissed this way when the stumps are hit before they complete a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Run out is a mode of dismissal in cricket and also means used up or exhausted.

definitions.meaning: a raised knob or ornament, as on a shield
a farm for breeding animals, such as horses

explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal Farm' looks like Orwell's novel but just means a farm where animals are bred.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a raised boss or knob and also an establishment where animals are bred.

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, so it sounds like a word for food

parts.note: meat is food, flesh eaten

explanation.surface: A server asks whether to hand out the food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives a word sounding like MEAT but spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to distribute or allot, as with punishment or rations, so to dole out.

clue.text: Additional insurance against being driven off

definitions.meaning: further cover in a policy
a cricket fielder placed to stop drives through the off side

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, this fielding position stands wide on the off side to stop the ball driven there by the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra cover is both additional insurance protection and a cricket fielding position against off-side drives.

definitions.meaning: snug and warm, comfortable
a padded cover placed over a teapot to keep it warm

explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' links the two: the item is comfortable, and it sits over the tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy means snug and comfortable; a cosy is also a cover put over a teapot.

clue.text: Put in a difficult position when a tip gave offence

parts.note: an end is a tip or extremity
angered means provoked, gave offence

explanation.surface: Someone got into trouble when a gratuity caused upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to put at risk, a difficult or dangerous position.
